## Root orb-249-peer-fixture: Preserve intended fixture results

Kind: group
Project: orbit
Parent: null
Depends on: none

Objective: Gateway's native WireGuard peer fixture reports the shell's intended result even when the child exits before reading all input, with bounded and cleanup-safe execution.

Scope:

- In: the test-only shell adapter in `apps/gateway/tests/Feature/Infrastructure/WireGuard/NativeWireGuardPeerConvergerTest.php` and its transport regression coverage. A narrow test-only helper extraction is allowed if needed to exercise the same adapter directly.
- Out: production WireGuard and SSH behavior, exit-code mapping, resolver policy, host pipe limits, test selection policy, caller-database protection, Incus harness code, fleet operations, maintained product documentation, dependencies, and unrelated test cleanup.

Shared context:

- Clean-main diagnosis found a 9,738-byte rewritten retain script sent to an 8,192-byte pipe. At baseline line 1867, raw `fwrite($pipes[0], $input)` can raise an EPIPE notice when Bash exits before consuming the remaining 1,546 bytes. Laravel converts that notice into `ErrorException`; the fixture never returns its `CommandResult`.
- The unchanged child exits 42 for stale retained recovery and 43 for each unsupported state. Existing production mappings already produce the required domain errors when they receive these results. Fixing those mappings or catching transport exceptions in production would miss this issue's objective.
- The adapter currently writes stdin, then drains stdout and stderr sequentially, then closes the child. The repair must address bounded input/output progress and cleanup, not only silence the reported warning. Keep Bash stdin execution, arguments, fixture cwd, path rewriting, and shim PATH behavior intact.
- Existing Symfony Process support and a private seekable input stream are feasible options. The worker chooses the narrow test-only design after inspecting installed APIs. No particular transport is mandated. File-backed stdin alone does not establish timeout, output-drain, or cleanup correctness.
- The diagnostic snapshot contains catch/drain/log/rethrow instrumentation, not a repair. Start from the admitted repository base. Do not copy its instrumentation into the candidate as a fix or treat replay results as candidate acceptance.
- Retained guidance passed 12 tests / 267 assertions at this baseline. The two retained full Gateway runs each had 7 failures: the six target failures and an unrelated private-ORBIT_HOME assertion mismatch. They also failed to persist a TIA graph. Preserve these facts; neither run is a green suite or a reusable cache baseline.
- Those diagnosis runs used the unfiltered Gateway configuration with `--tia --fresh`: they reproduced the fixture failures as part of a complete project run, not a fixture-only filtered run. They are distinct from future affected-candidate TIA in V1 and the clean exact-candidate five-project root gate in I2. No diagnostic run substitutes for either gate.

issue.title: Preserve early-exit results in the WireGuard test fixture
issue.description:
Gateway's native WireGuard peer tests report the shell's intended result even when it exits before reading all input. On main `317de2b630f7e8febdc3f2a25a664e10d14a6beb`, six assertions instead receive `ErrorException: fwrite(): Write of 1546 bytes failed with errno=32 Broken pipe`: the test adapter feeds a 9,738-byte script into an 8,192-byte pipe after Bash has taken its intended early exit.

## Scope

* In: the test-only shell adapter in `apps/gateway/tests/Feature/Infrastructure/WireGuard/NativeWireGuardPeerConvergerTest.php` and its transport regression coverage.
* Out: production WireGuard and SSH behavior, exit-code mapping, resolver policy, host pipe limits, test selection policy, caller-database protection, Incus harness code, and fleet operations.
* Out: maintained product documentation; this repair changes no product or operator contract.

## Acceptance

- [ ] The stale recoverable transaction case receives `NodeProvisioningException` with step `wireguard-peer-transaction` and code `vpn.peer_recovery_pending`; its retained-recovery and next-retry assertions still pass. Proof: Gateway TIA executes the existing stale-transaction case using the real local Bash fixture, whose observed child exit is 42.
- [ ] Each unsupported systemd state (`generated`, `transient`, `alias`, `linked`, `linked-runtime`) receives `NodeProvisioningException` with code `vpn.peer_state_unsupported`; existing no-mutation, DNS, service-state, and rollback assertions remain intact. Proof: Gateway TIA executes all five existing dataset rows using the real local fixture, whose observed child exits are 43.
- [ ] The test transport returns the intended exit code and output when a child exits before consuming input larger than a pipe buffer; successful input is complete, completion is bounded, and children and streams are cleaned up. Proof: automated local-process regressions cover early exit with large input, complete successful input, and bounded failure without suppressing unrelated errors or changing host limits.
- [ ] Existing peer success, rollback, and cleanup behavior remains tested; generic-failure assertions cannot conceal a transport exception in place of the intended shell result. Proof: Gateway affected TIA coverage exercises these paths and explicitly checks the expected result or domain error, without removing or weakening the existing assertions.
